# Japanese encephalitis

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Infectious diseases > Infections of the central nervous system > Japanese encephalitis*

[Original Article Link](/library/Hp0KIS)

---

## Summary

Japanese <u>encephalitis</u> is a mosquito-borne viral disease <u>endemic</u> in Asia and the Western Pacific. Disease transmission occurs through the bite of infected Culex tritaeniorhynchus mosquitoes. Clinically, <u>Japanese encephalitis virus</u> (<u>JEV</u>) infection can range from asymptomatic disease to acute <u>encephalitis</u>, which occurs in < 1% of patients. Despite its rarity, acute <u>encephalitis</u> with <u>altered mental status</u> and neurological deficits remains the most important clinical manifestation; it typically develops following a short period of non-specific <u>febrile</u> illness. <u>Seizures</u> are common, especially in children. Other known clinical manifestations include acute <u>psychosis</u> and <u>spastic</u> or <u>flaccid paralysis</u>. Elevations in <u>white blood cell count</u> and <u>CSF</u> <u>pleocytosis</u> are often present, along with characteristic thalamic lesions on <u>brain</u> <u>MRI</u>. Definitive diagnosis is made through <u>serology</u>. <u>Vaccinations</u> are available for travelers and as part of childhood <u>immunization</u> programs in some <u>endemic</u> areas.
